literal: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi
idiomatic: Pei Rangzhi; younger brothers Souzhi and Yanzhi; Huangfu He; Li Gou; Zhang Yanzhi; Lu Ang; Wang Songnian; Liu Yi

literal: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.
idiomatic: Pei Rangzhi, styled Shili.

literal: At age sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly beyond bearing; his mother the Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy your nature—could that make you a filial son?
idiomatic: At sixteen he lost his father, grief nearly more than he could bear; his mother Lady Xin wept as she comforted him, saying, "Would you abandon me and destroy yourself—could that make you a filial son?

literal: " Thereupon he urged himself on.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he forced himself to recover.

literal: Lady Xin was a lofty and clear exemplar among women, and also versed in ritual propriety.
idiomatic: Lady Xin was an exemplary woman of high principle and also well versed in ritual.

literal: When her husband died, the sons were mostly young and weak; she widely invited teachers and friends, or personally instructed them.
idiomatic: After her husband's death the sons were still young; she brought in many tutors or taught them herself.

literal: Kin within and without, for auspicious or inauspicious occasions and ritual rules, mostly took her as their model.
idiomatic: Relatives near and far took her as their model for ritual on happy and mournful occasions.

literal: Rangzhi from youth loved learning, had literary talent, sharp eloquence, and early won reputation.
idiomatic: Rangzhi loved learning from youth; gifted in letters and sharp in debate, he won an early reputation.

literal: In Wei times under Tianping he was recommended as xiucai; in policy responses he ranked at the top.
idiomatic: Under Wei in the Tianping era he was recommended as xiucai and ranked first in the policy examination.

literal: He rose repeatedly to Director of Agriculture and Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing; within the ministry they said, "Who can compose poetry? Pei Rangzhi.
idiomatic: He rose to director of agriculture and master of guests in the masters of writing; at court they said, "Who can write poetry? Pei Rangzhi.

literal: " He served as recorder for the Prince of Taiyuan's establishment.
idiomatic: " He became recorder on the staff of the Prince of Taiyuan.

literal: He was friendly with Yang Yin; when they met they held pure talk the whole day.
idiomatic: He was close to Yang Yin; whenever they met they talked the day away.

literal: Yin would often say, "This man's spirit is alert and outstanding—Pei Wenji is not dead after all.
idiomatic: Yin often said, "This man's spirit is striking and outstanding—Pei Wenji lives on in him.

literal: " When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi act as master of guests attendant.
idiomatic: " When a Liang envoy arrived, the emperor had Rangzhi serve as acting master of guests.

literal: His second younger brother Souzhi fled to Guanxi; all five brothers were detained.
idiomatic: His second brother Souzhi fled to the western passes; all five brothers were imprisoned.

literal: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?
idiomatic: Gao Huan asked, "Where is Souzhi?

literal: " He answered, "In former times Wu and Shu were two states, yet the Zhuge brothers each had his wish fulfilled; how much more when Rangzhi's old mother is here—ruler and minister roles are fixed; to lose both loyalty and filial piety is what a fool would not do.
idiomatic: " He answered, "Long ago Wu and Shu were two realms, yet the Zhuge brothers each got his way; all the more when Rangzhi's aged mother is here—lord and subject each have his place; to lose loyalty and filial piety together is what no fool would choose.

literal: I humbly wish the lord will treat things with sincerity and trust; if you treat things without trust, how can things in turn trust you?
idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, to meet the world with sincerity; if you meet the world without trust, how can the world trust you in return?

literal: To settle hegemony on this basis is like walking backward to seek the Way.
idiomatic: To found dominion on that is like walking backward to find the road.

literal: " Gao Huan approved his words, and the brothers were all released.
idiomatic: " Gao Huan approved his reply, and the brothers were all freed.

literal: He served successively as chief clerk to Gao Cheng as grand general, concurrently secretariat attendant, later concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and as envoy to Liang.
idiomatic: He served as chief clerk on Gao Cheng's staff as grand general, then as concurrent secretariat attendant and later as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on a mission to Liang.

literal: Gao Cheng once entered court; Rangzhi guided him in; his bearing was composed and refined; Gao Cheng looked at him and said, "Shili is a fine attendant.
idiomatic: Once when Gao Cheng went to court Rangzhi led him in with composed, refined bearing; Gao Cheng glanced at him and said, "Shili is a fine gentleman of the secretariat.

literal: " He was transferred to senior concurrent secretariat vice director, still holding attendant.
idiomatic: " He was promoted to senior concurrent secretariat vice director while retaining his attendant post.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, Emperor Jing withdrew to a separate palace to take leave of the ministers; Rangzhi wept and sobbed.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, Emperor Jing retired to a side palace to bid the ministers farewell; Rangzhi wept aloud.

literal: For helping manage ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningdu.
idiomatic: For helping draft ritual regulations he was enfeoffed as baron of Ningdu county.

literal: The emperor wished to make him yellow gate attendant; some said his body was too heavy and he could not bear hurrying in attendance, so he was instead made grand administrator of Qinghe.
idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him yellow gate attendant, but some said he was too heavyset for palace attendance, so he was made grand administrator of Qinghe instead.

literal: Not long after he reached the commandery, Yang Yin said to Rangzhi's younger brothers, "Your worthy elder brother and I are close in friendship; I look forward to hearing of good government.
idiomatic: Soon after he took office in the commandery, Yang Yin told Rangzhi's brothers, "Your elder brother and I are close; I have been eager to hear of his good rule.

literal: Just now someone came from Qinghe and said corrupt clerks have drawn in their claws and bandits are quiet.
idiomatic: Someone has just arrived from Qinghe saying corrupt officials have pulled back and robbers are subdued.

literal: The target of a full month has been overturned still faster.
idiomatic: What should have taken a month has come about even sooner.

literal: " In Qinghe were two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuangui and Sun Shexing—long-serving, crafty and slippery, who often shaved off shares and, using incidents, then extorted people's wealth.
idiomatic: " Qinghe had two powerful clerks, Tian Zhuanggui and Sun Shexing—veteran, cunning officials who often skimmed funds and used any pretext to extort money.

literal: Calculating the booty by law did not reach death.
idiomatic: By law the amount of stolen goods did not warrant death.

literal: Rangzhi, because they had disrupted the law, killed them.
idiomatic: Rangzhi executed them for subverting the law.

literal: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was inspector of Si province; he sent a bureau aide to investigate the case.
idiomatic: At the time Prince Yue of Qinghe was governor of Si province and sent a staff investigator to review the case.

literal: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long been at odds with Rangzhi; in the memorial of investigation he said, "When Your Majesty received the mandate, Rangzhi cherished the Wei court, sobbed and wept; compared with being an inner-court official, his heart was not in it.
idiomatic: Palace attendant Gao Dezheng had long disliked Rangzhi; in his report he wrote, "When Your Majesty took the throne, Rangzhi clung to the Wei house and wept; service at court was not what he wished.

literal: " Before long Yang Yin pleaded for his life, saying, "The crime does not merit death.
idiomatic: " Yang Yin then pleaded for him, saying, "The offense does not deserve death.

literal: " Gao Yang was greatly enraged and said to Yin, "Do you wish to share a tomb with Pei Rangzhi?
idiomatic: " Gao Yang flew into a rage and said to Yin, "Do you want to lie in the same grave as Pei Rangzhi?

literal: " Thereupon none dared speak further.
idiomatic: " After that no one dared speak up.

literal: When the matter was reported, in the end he was ordered to die at home.
idiomatic: When the case was finalized, he was ordered to take his own life at home.

literal: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.
idiomatic: Rangzhi's next younger brother was Souzhi.

literal: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, from youth loved Confucian learning; on leaving the robe he became erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: Souzhi, styled Shizheng, loved Confucian studies from youth and on first office became an erudite of the Imperial Academy.

literal: He once borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in some ten days.
idiomatic: Once he borrowed a hundred scrolls from Chang Jing and returned them in about ten days.

literal: Jing suspected he had not read them; he questioned him on each scroll, and he answered without omission.
idiomatic: Jing doubted he could have read them and quizzed him scroll by scroll; he answered without a gap.

literal: Jing sighed and said, "Ying Feng could take in the Five Classics at once, Mi Heng remembered on a single reading—today I see it again in Master Pei.
idiomatic: Jing sighed, "Ying Feng took in the Five Classics at a stroke and Mi Heng remembered at one glance—today the same gift appears in Master Pei.

literal: " When Yang Yin had his whole clan reburied, he entrusted Souzhi to dash off more than ten epitaphs at once; the texts were all worth reading.
idiomatic: " When Yang Yin reburied his entire clan, he had Souzhi write more than ten epitaphs in quick succession, each of them presentable.

literal: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's younger brother Liang were all famed in Luoyang; people of the time said, "Souzhi surpasses Rangzhi; He is not the equal of Liang.
idiomatic: Rangzhi, Souzhi, and Huangfu He's brother Liang were all famous in Luoyang; contemporaries said, "Souzhi outdoes Rangzhi; He cannot match Liang.

literal: " Minister of Works Gao Gan sent a letter saying, "I would bend you to serve as household census aide.
idiomatic: " Minister of works Gao Gan wrote inviting him to serve as household census aide.

literal: " Souzhi replied by letter and would not accept appointment.
idiomatic: " Souzhi answered by letter and declined the post.

literal: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was summoned as recorder.
idiomatic: When Prince Kai of Pei opened his grand marshal's office, Souzhi was recruited as recorder.

literal: After the move to Ye, Souzhi remained in Henan; Western Wei commanding general Dugu Xin entered and seized Jinyong, made Souzhi staff officer of his office, and styled him "the surviving worthy of Luoyang.
idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, Souzhi stayed in Henan; Western Wei's commanding general Dugu Xin seized Jinyong, appointed Souzhi to his staff, and called him "the last eminent man of Luoyang.

literal: " When Xin was defeated, Souzhi lived on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui summoned him as central aide.
idiomatic: " After Xin was defeated, Souzhi dwelt on South Mountain; Luoyang inspector Wang Yuangui appointed him central aide.

literal: Western troops suddenly arrived, then soon withdrew; he thereupon followed the western army into the passes.
idiomatic: Western troops came suddenly and soon withdrew; he then followed the western army through the passes into Guanzhong.

literal: Prince Wen of Zhou made him director of granaries on the Grand Mobile Staff; he died in office.
idiomatic: Prince Wen of Zhou appointed him director of granaries on the grand mobile staff; he died in that post.

literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Xu province.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Xu province.

literal: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, at seven sui was already diligent in study and early won fame.
idiomatic: Yanzhi, styled Shiping, was studying hard by age seven and was known early.

literal: He rose repeatedly to chief clerk of the Ministry of Education.
idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk in the ministry of education.

literal: Yang Yin would often praise him, saying, "Among the gentry clans of Hedong there are many capital officials, but only this household's brothers have no trace of home accent.
idiomatic: Yang Yin often praised him, saying, "Hedong has many families with capital officials, but only these brothers speak without a hometown accent.

literal: Though Yanzhi was still young, he did not make friends lightly; only Longxi Xin Shu, Zhao commandery Li Hui, Dunqiu Li Gou, and Qinghe Cui Zhan were his friends across the years.
idiomatic: Though still young, Yanzhi did not socialize lightly; only Xin Shu of Longxi, Li Hui of Zhao commandery, Li Gou of Dunqiu, and Cui Zhan of Qinghe were his friends despite the age gap.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was about to return to Ye, he was transferred to gentleman of the rituals bureau; he especially knew past dynasties' precedents and ritual regulations, and could correct all mourning rites.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao's coffin was to return to Ye, he was made gentleman of the rituals bureau; he knew dynastic precedent and ceremonial law especially well and could set right every mourning rite.

literal: As grand administrator of Yongchang, when travelers passed through the commandery he supplied them from private funds; where the district had nothing, he advanced payment on their behalf, and the clerks and people were grateful.
idiomatic: As grand administrator of Yongchang, he paid traveling guests from his own purse when the commandery had nothing on hand, advancing funds for them in advance, and officials and commoners alike were grateful.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou's service and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.
idiomatic: After Qi fell he served Zhou and died as grand administrator of Yichuan.

literal: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was a man of Chaona in Anding; his ancestors because of office had taken residence in Hanzhong.
idiomatic: Huangfu He, styled Changxie, was from Chaona in Anding; his forebears had settled in Hanzhong through official postings.

literal: His grandfather Cheng was inspector of Qin and Liang in Southern Qi.
idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had been inspector of Qin and Liang under Southern Qi.

literal: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, was grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.
idiomatic: His father Hui, styled Zixuan, had been grand administrator of Anding and Lüeyang in Liang.

literal: In the second year of Zhengshi in Wei, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian in entering Wei; Daoqian separately submitted a merit roster wishing to list Hui as chief conspirator.
idiomatic: In Wei, second year of Zhengshi, he followed his wife's father Xiahou Daoqian into Wei service; Daoqian filed a separate merit roll naming Hui as chief plotter.

literal: Hui said, "At the beginning of the plot I had no part in it; though I covet glory and reward, inwardly I am ashamed.
idiomatic: Hui said, "I took no part when the plot began; though I crave honor and reward, my conscience would not bear it.

literal: " He therefore refused and would not accept.
idiomatic: " He refused and would not accept.

literal: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou valued his honesty and substance and memorialized him as staff officer of the campaign against barbarians; he died in office.
idiomatic: Liang inspector Yang Lingyou respected his solid character and recommended him as staff officer on the campaign against barbarians; he died in that post.

literal: He at eleven was orphaned; his mother the Lady Xiahou was talented, clear, and observant of ritual propriety, and personally taught him the classics.
idiomatic: He was orphaned at eleven; his mother Lady Xiahou was talented, principled, and versed in ritual, and taught him the classics herself.

literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, with refined capacity, especially clear in ritual propriety; kin far and near on auspicious or inauspicious occasions mostly sought his counsel.
idiomatic: As an adult he was grave and measured, especially skilled in ritual; relatives consulted him on happy and mournful occasions.

literal: He died as grand administrator of Jiyin.
idiomatic: He died while serving as grand administrator of Jiyin.

literal: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was a man of Liyang.
idiomatic: Li Gou, styled Zuji, was from Liyang.

literal: His grandfather Ping was vice director of the masters of writing in Wei.
idiomatic: His grandfather Ping had been vice director of the masters of writing under Wei.

literal: Gou from youth was praised for uprightness; on leaving the robe he became staff officer of an opening office, rose repeatedly to inspector of Qiao, and died in office.
idiomatic: Gou was known from youth for rectitude; on first appointment he joined an opening office staff, rose to inspector of Qiao, and died there.

literal: Gou's younger cousin by the father's line was Shu; in Wei he was son of the grand minister of agriculture Xie.
idiomatic: Gou's younger cousin on the father's side was Shu, son of Wei grand minister of agriculture Xie.

literal: Correct and elegant, he loved learning, had refined standards of conduct, and bore a strong family style.
idiomatic: Refined and fond of learning, he kept strict standards of conduct and upheld the family reputation.

literal: He rose gradually to magistrate of Linzhang.
idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to magistrate of Linzhang.

literal: When the History of Wei appeared, Shu together with Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others sued over its unfairness and were all imprisoned.
idiomatic: When the History of Wei was published, Shu joined Lu Fei, Wang Songnian, and others in suing over its bias and was imprisoned with them.

literal: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong called himself a man of Taiyuan, and also said Wang Qiong was poor at serving;
idiomatic: Wei Shou wrote that Wang Huilong claimed to be from Taiyuan and also said Wang Qiong was inept in his duties;

literal: Lu Tong was attached to the biography of Lu Xuan;
idiomatic: Lu Tong was tucked into the biography of Lu Xuan;

literal: Li Ping was made a man of Chenliu, saying his family was poor and base.
idiomatic: Li Ping was called a man of Chenliu and described as coming from a poor, humble house.

literal: Therefore the Pei clan and others brought the suit, saying to Yang Yin, "Wei Shou ought to be put to death.
idiomatic: Hence the Pei party and others brought suit, telling Yang Yin, "Wei Shou deserves execution.

literal: " Yin sided with Wei Shou; they thereupon reported to Gao Yang that Fei and the others were guilty, and all were shaved and given two hundred lashes.
idiomatic: " Yin took Wei Shou's side; they then denounced Fei and the rest to Gao Yang, and all were shaved and flogged two hundred strokes.

literal: Shu died in Linzhang prison; Shu's elder brother Yue grieved for him and to the end of his life never passed Linzhang's county gate.
idiomatic: Shu died in Linzhang jail; his elder brother Yue mourned him so deeply that he never again went through Linzhang's gate while he lived.

literal: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.
idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhi, styled Xide.

literal: Orphaned young, he had utmost nature; his mother the Lady Zheng taught and admonished him, and in action he always followed the ritual canon.
idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was deeply dutiful; his mother Lady Zheng raised him by the rites, and he followed them in everything.

literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in pacifying Yuan Hao, was given the enfeoffment Baron of Wucheng, and rose repeatedly to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.
idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Yuan Hao, was enfeoffed baron of Wucheng, and rose to gentleman of the two-thousand-dan rank in the masters of writing.

literal: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again made Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.
idiomatic: When Gao Yue campaigned in Yingchuan, he again appointed Yanzhi commanding aide of central troops with concurrent recorder.

literal: Yanzhi was a man of letters who also had martial ability; he often joined Yue in planning within the curtains, and also often took short weapons to clash at close quarters, personally taking heads—deeply admired by Yue.
idiomatic: Yanzhi was a literatus with martial skill; he often joined Yue's council in the tent and just as often fought hand to hand with a short blade, taking heads himself—much to Yue's admiration.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang took Yanzhi's daughter as consort and ordered Yanzhi to go to Jinyang to complete the rites.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao, Gao Yang as Prince of Gaoyang married Yanzhi's daughter and ordered him to Jinyang to finish the wedding.

literal: Afterward in the rear garden he attended a feast; seated guests all composed poetry.
idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the rear garden, every guest was asked to compose a poem.

literal: Yanzhi's poem said, "When the realm has the Way, the lord is bright and ministers upright; though there is rest, do not rest—forever leave a model to the age.
idiomatic: Yanzhi's poem ran, "When the Way holds the realm, the ruler is bright and his ministers straight; though all is calm, do not grow calm—leave the age a lasting model.

literal: " Gao Yang laughed and said, "To gain your admonition in verse deeply comforts my heart.
idiomatic: " Gao Yang laughed and said, "Your verse of counsel comforts me deeply.

literal: " Later he acted for North Xu province and soon received the full appointment; officials and people loved him.
idiomatic: " He later administered North Xu province, soon received the regular appointment, and was beloved by officials and people.

literal: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected the provinces and commanderies; reaching North Xu he found nothing to impeach, only several pieces of "Pure Virtue Praise" composed by the common people.
idiomatic: Censor Cui Ziwu inspected provinces and commanderies; at North Xu he found no charges to bring, only several "Hymns of Pure Virtue" written by the people.

literal: He thereupon sighed and said, "I came seeking crimes and instead heard songs of praise.
idiomatic: He sighed, "I came looking for offenses and instead heard praise.

literal: " He was transferred to inspector of Yan province; before he could take up the post he died.
idiomatic: " He was transferred to inspector of Yan but died before assuming the post.

literal: Posthumously he was given inspector of Qi province.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Qi province.

literal: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.
idiomatic: Lu Ang, styled Yunju.

literal: From youth he was quick and perceptive, of fine spirit and bearing; he loved learning without tiring, broadly reading many books, and mostly penetrated the great meaning of the Five Classics.
idiomatic: From youth he was quick and perceptive, handsome in spirit and bearing; he studied tirelessly, read widely, and grasped the main sense of the Five Classics.

literal: Skilled at composing literature, he was greatly prized by Xing Shao of Hejian.
idiomatic: Skilled in writing, he was greatly admired by Xing Shao of Hejian.
